title: Industry ML Pipeline
blurb: The fuller lifecycle as it runs in practice.

ladders.title: Industry ML Pipeline
ladders.prompt: Order the pipeline as it actually runs in an organisation.

steps.label: Understand the Business Problem and Stakeholders
steps.detail: Who is affected, who decides, and what a good outcome is for them. Skipping this is how technically sound models get built for the wrong problem.

steps.label: Define the ML Task, Constraints, and Success Metrics
steps.detail: Fix the target, the latency and cost budget, and the metric before any data is touched, so success cannot be redefined after the fact.

steps.label: Source Data and Establish Governance
steps.detail: Establish lawful basis, licence, consent and retention up front. Data acquired without them is a liability that no later step removes.

steps.label: Ingest, Catalogue, and Version Data
steps.detail: Land the data with a catalogue entry and a version. Without versioning no result is reproducible and no regression is explainable.

steps.label: Explore Data and Validate Quality
steps.detail: Profile distributions, nulls, duplicates and outliers before modelling, because every one of them shows up later as unexplained error.

steps.label: Clean, Transform, and Label Data
steps.detail: Repair what can be repaired and label what needs labels, with the labelling guidance itself treated as a versioned artefact.

steps.label: Engineer and Select Features
steps.detail: Build the representations the model will use, and drop the ones that leak the target or will not exist at inference time.

steps.label: Create Training, Validation, and Test Splits
steps.detail: Split before fitting anything, respecting time and group boundaries. A split made after preprocessing has already leaked.

steps.label: Build a Reproducible Baseline
steps.detail: A simple model that runs end to end. It sets the bar every later candidate must clear and proves the pipeline works.

steps.label: Train Candidate Models and Track Experiments
steps.detail: Fit alternatives with their configuration, data version and results recorded, so the winner can be rebuilt months later.

steps.label: Tune Hyperparameters with Validation Data
steps.detail: Search settings against validation data only. Tuning against test data turns the final number into self-assessment.

steps.label: Evaluate Quality, Robustness, Fairness, and Security
steps.detail: Test held-out quality, behaviour under perturbation, performance by subgroup, and adversarial exposure. One aggregate accuracy number hides all three of the others.

steps.label: Document, Approve, Package, and Register the Model
steps.detail: Record intended use, limits and evaluation results, get the accountable approval, and register the artefact. This is what makes deployment reviewable.

steps.label: Deploy Gradually with Automated Tests and Rollback
steps.detail: Shadow, canary or staged rollout with a tested path back. Gradual exposure is what makes a bad release survivable.

steps.label: Monitor Data, Model, System, and Business Performance
steps.detail: Watch all four layers. Inputs drift, quality decays, infrastructure fails and business value erodes — and they are not the same signal.

steps.label: Collect Feedback, Retrain, Revalidate, or Retire
steps.detail: Feed production reality back in, and decide deliberately between retraining, revalidating and retirement. A model with no retirement criterion never gets retired.
